topic: Time Expressions (In a short time vs. In a few time)
said: Maybe in a few time, we can increase the salaries
natural: In the near future / Soon, we will be able to raise salaries
why: 'Time' as continuous duration is uncountable, so we say 'in a short time' or 'in the near future', never 'in a few time'. In economic contexts, 'raise salaries' is the standard institutional phrasing.

said: People can came... they can't came easily
natural: People can come... they cannot come easily
why: Modal auxiliary verbs (can, could, should, must, will) must always be followed directly by the base bare infinitive ('come'), never the past simple form ('came').

said: I trust on you in that story
natural: I trust you on that story / I believe you regarding that story
why: The verb 'trust' takes a direct personal object ('I trust you'). To anchor your trust to a particular statement or event, connect with 'on' ('I trust you on that matter').

topic: Hypothetical Conditionals (Would panic vs. Be in panic)
said: I don't know how you can to live there... I probably be in panic
natural: I don't know how you can live there... I would probably panic / I'd be in a total panic
why: Omit 'to' after modal 'can' ('how you can live'). When imagining hypothetical reactions to extreme situations, use conditional 'would' ('I would probably panic').

topic: Comparative Quantifiers (Much more vs. Too much)
said: I have too much CV that the others... only for work abroad I have too much experience than the others
natural: I have a much stronger CV than the others... just by working abroad, I have far more experience than them
why: 'Too much' implies an excessive negative defect ('too much debt'). In positive comparative statements, use 'far more experience than' or 'a much stronger CV'. Prepositions require the gerund ('by working abroad').
